question: Why does a Stellar account not exist until funded, what minimum activates it, and why do payments to a brand-new address fail as not found or not activated?

golden.answer: A keypair is only an identity until a CreateAccount operation creates its ledger entry, so a Payment to a nonexistent G-address fails with PAYMENT_NO_DESTINATION. An unsponsored empty account needs two base reserves, 1 XLM at the 0.5 XLM base reserve, which validators can change. A sponsored CreateAccount (CAP-0033) can use startingBalance 0.
keyFacts: CreateAccount, not key generation or Payment, creates the ledger account.
The unsponsored minimum is two base reserves (1 XLM at the 0.5 XLM reserve).
Sponsored creation can start at 0 XLM.
avoid: Do NOT say Payment creates a missing destination or that every generated address exists.
golden.notes: Accept 1 XLM only when dated or tied to the reserve; the reserve is validator-set.

corroboration.claim: CreateAccount creates the ledger account; an unsponsored empty account currently needs two reserves, while sponsored creation may use startingBalance=0 and shift reserve responsibility to the sponsor.
